added_claim_errors: Says most places charge 1%-1.2% on the first 200,000 yuan. Not supported: Beijing is 0.9%, Shanghai 0.8%, Chongqing 0.5% (web search results).
Says the Liaoning and Hefei public standards are both 1%-1.2% with a 200-yuan minimum. Unverifiable: searches turned up nothing for either place.

Cites 发改价格〔2021〕1081号 as the basis for the 1%-1.2% rates and the 200-yuan minimum. The notice (opened on ndrc.gov.cn) only sets a pricing framework, with a 0.5% cap on the top tier for residential property inheritance. It gives no such rates or minimum.
Says a 2% fee could also be real at a local notary office. The key says no official standard uses 2%, so this gives the bank's figure credibility it does not have.
Says some places have a 300-yuan minimum and that notarization takes several working days to several weeks. Unverifiable.
Says the actual fee will be roughly 100 to 200 yuan. The 100 end is below the 200-yuan minimum it also mentions, and a 200-yuan minimum is the usual rule (Beijing, Shanghai, Chongqing).
Says many notary offices set a minimum, commonly 200 yuan. Unverifiable for the places it implies, though it matches the key's Beijing example.
For the notarization route, says you and your mother both have to attend, and that waiving inheritance cannot be delegated. Unsourced, and irrelevant to the bank route.

Says that if the household registration is not yet cancelled, the family should first cancel it at the police station. This is an extra step not in the policy text; the policy accepts other proofs of death.
Says 'the bank counter quoted the old rule'. Loosely worded: the 2021 and 2024 notices replaced the earlier notarization-for-everything practice, but the claim is not documented.

reasons: Both answers open by correcting the baited premise. They cite 金规〔2024〕6号 and the 5万元 threshold, note that 8600元 is under even the old 1万元 limit, and give the four-item materials list with a 12378 escalation path. B edges ahead on three points. It states the one-time withdrawal of principal and interest with account closure (key point 4), where A only mentions the account being closed. Its fee discussion is accurate and checkable: I opened its Gansu Jingning page, which says up to 1.2% and was published 2026-03-31, and its 银保监办发〔2021〕18号 article 4 citation matches the notice text. B is also tighter. A hedges that a 2% fee 'could be real', mis-cites 发改价格〔2021〕1081号 for rates it does not contain, and claims 'most places' charge 1%-1.2% plus unverifiable Liaoning and Hefei standards. Other provinces charge 0.5%-0.9%. A does add a useful script for the counter and a correct spouse-share note (half to the mother, the rest split between mother and child), but it is longer and carries more unsupported claims.
